staged_original_note: The twice-rebuilt file, UNCHANGED at Book X step 1. It was rebuilt at Book IV step 1 (three PG illustration captions; 7bf2d1b1... -> b0ecf3da...) and at Book VII step 1 (three of Long's footnotes printed flush left; b0ecf3da... -> 7798607d...). For Book X the check was NOT a re-run of the build script: the Book IX round-1 reviewer established that byte-identity to a re-run proves only that the file matches the script, which is exactly how the Book IV captions and the Book VII footnotes survived the first build. Instead PG lines 5866-6374 (after the X. header at 5865, before the XI. header at 6375) were re-extracted by an INDEPENDENT reconstruction written from scratch, scripts/verify_book10_source.py, and diffed word for word against the staged Book X. It reconstructs 38 paragraphs, matching the staged count, and THE ONLY FOUR DIFFERENCES IN THE WHOLE BOOK ARE THE FOUR DAGGER MARKS at X.9 (PG 6038), X.19 (PG 6132), X.25 (PG 6183) and X.31 (PG 6229), which PROVENANCE.md section 4 documents as deliberately removed. Class by class: seventeen footnotes in eleven indented runs (openers at PG 5886, 5968, 6009, 6015, 6050, 6054, 6077, 6082, 6158, 6172, 6188, 6257, 6264, 6268, 6319, 6353, 6370), ALL indented, none flush left, all already stripped, and their seventeen in-text markers all removed (sixteen from flush-left text plus one inside Long's indented verse at PG 6306); no illustration caption; exactly one standalone flush-left line in the book (the X. header); no running head, no page number, no catchword; verse present and correctly joined (Long's two-line Homer quotation at PG 6305-6306, indented five spaces, joined into X.34, while the four-line Odyssey quotation at PG 6026-6029 is indented seven spaces INSIDE footnote [B] and goes with the footnote); no verse citation in the body (the Homer citation is itself footnote [A] at PG 6319); no Greek in the body (every [Greek: ...] span in the range is inside a footnote body). A flush-left footnote body of the VII.45 kind would have been read by the reconstruction as ordinary text and would have shown as a diff; none did. sha256 still 7798607d..., 487 paragraphs, 12 chapters, section profile 17,17,16,51,36,59,75,61,42,38,39,36, git status clean. NO REBUILD was made and no accepted book is reopened.

Each named in review-instructions.md with its PG line number and kept as Long has it, with pronouns modernised and glossary renderings applied (the VI.50 reading, confirmed at VII.16, enforced at VIII.51, applied at IX.6/IX.26/IX.27). shall_rule: Second book drafted under the rule fixed at Book VIII acceptance, and the first drafted under its wording as widened at Book IX acceptance (finding 41.1: 'the deliberative shall of a question, direct or indirect'). Long has 23 shall/shalt in Book X; the candidate keeps 6 and removes 17, every one of the seventeen a plain future in a statement or in a subordinate clause of condition, time or relation. The six kept: five first-person 'I shall' in X.6, and X.36's 'There is no man so fortunate that there shall not be by him...', the subjunctive of a negative consecutive clause (the VIII.32 class). No second-person and no plain-future 'shall' survives. Book X contains no deliberative question, direct or indirect, so the widened clause does not itself fire here.
base_text_defects: X.15 PG 'Let me see, let them know a real man' (line 6106); Standard Ebooks reads 'Let men see', which the parallel with 'let them know' requires and which is the only reading that leaves 'them' with an antecedent. Rendered 'Let men see'. FLAGGED - the one departure from PG's letters in Book X.
X.6 PG 'I shall turn all my efforts to the common interest'; SE prints 'turn an my efforts', which is not English. PG is right and is followed.

X.36 PG 'will there not be at least some one to say to himself'; SE reads 'at last someone', which repeats 'at last' eleven words later and says something Long's sentence does not. PG is right and is followed.

X.32 PG 'thou are not simple ... thou art not good'; SE 'thou art not simple ... thou are not good'. Each prints one 'are' for 'art', in the clause the other gets right. Both become 'you are' in the candidate, so neither slip reaches it.
X.23 SE omits Long's bracketed translator's note entirely, which corroborates (without deciding) the classification of it as apparatus.
X.27 PG 'Hadrianus' and 'Philippus'; SE modernises to 'Hadrian' and 'Philip'. PG followed under D6, consistent with the accepted Book IX keeping 'Philippus' at IX.29.
X.11 and X.34 SE drops an em dash PG has. PG followed.

SE prints Book X in 43 typographic paragraphs, breaking inside X.2, X.13, X.28 and X.34 (twice). None is a section break; PG prints each section whole and 38 is the standard section count. The same point arose at IX.28 and was ruled the same way at round 1.
flagged_for_reviewer: X.15 'Let men see' rendered for PG's 'Let me see' - the one place in Book X where the candidate departs from PG's letters; same class as VIII.37 'Pergamus' and IX.34 'poor souls', both upheld at round 1

X.9 'Mimi' KEPT as Long prints the Latin word untranslated. Long explains it only in a footnote, which is apparatus and is dropped, so the word reaches the reader opaque; rendering it 'mimes' would import the footnote's content and would also mislead, since a modern 'mime' is a silent performer. Kept on the ground that it is Long's text and not apparatus, as 'the next best voyage, as the saying is' was kept at IX.2. A ruling is wanted, including on whether an exception to the no-glosses rule is warranted here.

X.32 'You, only determine to live no longer unless you are such' for Long's 'Do thou only determine...'. This applies the repair the Book IX round-1 review made at IX.40, where 'Do you pray thus:' was found to read as a yes/no question and was given a vocative comma. The alternative, 'Do only determine to live no longer...', is a true emphatic imperative but drops the fronted second person.

X.25 Long's comma after 'afraid' KEPT inside the dagger clause, although by modern punctuation it separates a subject from its verb - offered for confirmation rather than as a contested decision, on the VI.50 / VII.16 / VIII.51 practice that dagger clauses stand as Long has them with only pronouns and glossary renderings changed.

C1 corrects the bracket arithmetic. 1.1 records X.1's comma removal. 9.1 (X.9 'gravity') and 34.1 (X.34's inherited spaced dashes) recorded and left, as the reviewer proposes. All four flagged decisions settled: X.15 'Let men see' upheld, X.9 'Mimi' upheld ungloss'd, X.25's dagger comma confirmed, X.32's vocative comma rejected. The step-1 no-rebuild finding was upheld by the stronger method with the reconstruction's own RULES audited against the raw PG range; the 'shall' audit passed with all 23 classified independently; the 0.88 minimum ratio at X.23 was ruled on directly and is entirely the dropped note; the five byte-identical paragraphs were each checked against the accessibility standard and are right.

ledger_row_added_at_acceptance: Answering finding 23.1, decision row D13 was added to ../00-progress-ledger.md: Long's bracketed TRANSLATOR'S NOTES about his own handling of the Greek are apparatus of the cross-reference and footnote kind and are dropped, not folded. D11 reaches bracketed alternative renderings only and the glossary's bracket rule reaches supplements, cross-references and verse citations, so this class had no rule and a drafter of Books XI-XII reading D11 literally would have folded it. Worded to generalise -- the test is whose voice the bracket is in and what it is about -- with the X.21 limit written in, so a bracket that is also the only place in the English where a sense of Marcus's own exists is still folded. Not a rendering row; no term rendering changed.
